notes: OBLIVION-FEEL ADDITION (feel/build, the Barks lane), and it obeys the rule every other bark file does: NOTHING in the code writes a spoken line. The Watch & Rhythm lane keyed watch.halt from tickWatch and let it fall through to watch.demand until the row was on the sheet; the stance lane's standBack and joinBrawl had nobody saying anything. These are the three keys, in the ward's own register -- the impound keeper, the boards, the Flame, the Tarwalk -- and never a borrowed line from anybody else's game. watch.halt is what a watchman says the second he SEES steel or a corpse (WatchCause::Violence; he is Closing, the arrest follows at reach). brawl.join is a patron or a bouncer stepping into a fight the player started (joinBrawl; the Closing watchman keeps his own halt and a rat says nothing). crowd.flee is the panic line -- a patron sent back on the escalation edge, a bloodied man routing for the street, and the street itself through wardMoodKey while WardPolicy::Flee holds (mood.panicked, the owner's own, is the floor under it). Rows are severity-neutral on purpose: the same sheet serves a drawn blade and a killing, because neither speaker is told which. Rotation is the caller's index through BarkTables::line, so a night does not repeat itself. Plain ASCII only (Glyph8x8Font). Loaded after the owner's barks.json, so it can never take a key of his.

rows: Put it down. Put it down and stand where you are.
That is enough. I saw the whole of it and so did the room.
Steel in the Gull, in front of me. Stand still. Nobody walks out of this one.
Hold there. Whatever he did, the ward hangs you for that and not him.
Stand off him. I have seen it, and it is mine now.
Right. Then it is me as well.
You swung in Venn's house. Now there are two of us.
In this room you fight everybody, friend.
Get back. Get back from him.
Flame keep us. Do not look at him. Walk.
Not tonight. Not for a stranger. Move!
Somebody fetch the Watch. Somebody who is not me.
